title: Use do.call in ave() to avoid plyr::id
description: This is the final PR for dropping {plyr}. Here we just take advantage of `...` in `ave()` to accomplish what `id()` was used for.

title: refactor plyr::ddply usage
description: Made a choice to switch to a {base} equivalent here as opposed to {dplyr}, maybe that's not the right decision. Because of the problem of `split()` dropping missing levels, we have some extra overhead here -- I don't have enough context to know if that defensive coding is needed. The diff would look cleaner if we could ignore the `NA` case.

title: Implement rename() internally
description: In particular, respect the `message()` / `warning()` structure of unexpected input signals as `plyr::rename()` does.

title: Remove plyr::unrowname()
description: This helper is pretty simple, thankfully. Much less knotty to refactor.

title: Remove dlply() usage
description:
Here's a case where, for full generality, the {base} equivalent is painful enough to have warranted a Bugzilla filing.

Very closely related: https://github.com/haleyjeppson/ggmosaic/pull/80/files

title: Refactor ldply() and rbind.fill() out of divide()
description: Includes the tests in #14. This may be easier if using `bind_rows()` instead of re-rolling an `rbind.fill()` equivalent, but sticking with the old dependency structure for now.

title: Add prodcalc regression tests
description:
This is towards bolstering our confidence in any proposed refactoring of divide() away from using ldply(), rbind.fill().

Gemini basically wrote these. I asked the LLM to write an extensive test suite, and copy-pasted the output. A number of tests were wrong; I cleaned those up to match the `HEAD` behavior in any such case.

title: Use vapply() over ldply
description:
Related to #12 refactoring of {plyr} code

Not touching this last usage, which is much more involved / probably requires some unit testing:

https://github.com/hadley/productplots/blob/212ed698851e3c9e85c66cea72e7a9b4646c2748/R/divide.r#L25-L33

I'll do so in a separate PR for clarity.

title: Remove llply usage
description:
Sharing edits made to any CRAN packages as part of a migration away from {plyr}.

We are taking a gradual approach to facilitate back-compatibility. For code not using arguments like `.progress`, just switching back to `lapply()` is identical, AFAICT.

title: Add mapping parameter to draw function
description:
Allow mapping variables to `colour`, `fill`, `alpha`, etc. by adding a `mapping` parameter to the `draw` function, while keeping the default of `colour = "grey30"` in case colour is neither mapped to a variable nor given as a constant argument. The default of `alpha = 1` is standard anyway and therefore not needed. 

Example: 

```
prodplot(happy, ~ happy + marital + sex, mapping=aes(fill=sex, alpha=happy))
```

title: fix #2
description: I'm lazy to figure out the functions used in productplots to import explicitly; I just imported the whole package. Hope this is OK for #2.

title: I'm not sure if this behavior is intentional or not, but prodplot(happy, ~ happy, 'tile') does not work because two rectangles had the same left boundary and ddply was only splitting by left boundaries in col_labels.
description:
prodplot(happy, ~ happy, 'tile')
did not work due to two groups having the same left boundary and ddply was only splitting by left boundaries in col_labels.
